questions.prompt: Which of the following is the correct SI unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: Electric current is a fundamental quantity whose SI unit is the ampere (A).

questions.prompt: A car keeps a steady velocity of 18 m/s along a straight road. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Constant velocity means the velocity does not change, so a = (v - u)/t = 0 m/s².

questions.topic: Force and Newton's Laws of Motion
questions.prompt: Which everyday situation is the best example of inertia?
options: Coins on a card staying put when the card is flicked away
questions.explanation: Inertia is the tendency to resist a change in motion. The coins stay at rest when the card is flicked because of their inertia (Newton's First Law).

questions.prompt: The SI unit of power is the:
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work, measured in watts (W), where 1 W = 1 J/s.

questions.prompt: Why does a wide tractor tyre stop the tractor sinking into soft soil?
options: It has a large area, so it gives a smaller pressure
It has a small area, so it gives a larger pressure
It removes the force of gravity
questions.explanation: Since P = F/A, spreading the weight over a larger area lowers the pressure on the soil, so the tyre does not sink.

questions.prompt: What name is given to the transfer of heat through a solid metal bar from particle to particle?
questions.explanation: Heat passing through a solid from particle to particle, without the material itself moving, is conduction. Metals are good conductors.

questions.prompt: Convert a time of 2.5 hours into seconds.
A liquid has a mass of 0.8 kg and a volume of 0.001 m³. What is its density?
questions.explanation: Density = mass ÷ volume = 0.8 ÷ 0.001 = 800 kg/m³.

questions.prompt: A swimmer covers 90 m in 45 s at a steady pace. What is the average speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 90 ÷ 45 = 2 m/s.

questions.prompt: A scooter speeds up from 3 m/s to 21 m/s in 9 s. What is its acceleration?

questions.topic: Force and Newton's Laws of Motion
questions.prompt: A net force of 21 N acts on a 7 kg crate. What is its acceleration?

questions.topic: Force and Newton's Laws of Motion
questions.prompt: Using g = 9.8 m/s², what is the weight of a 4 kg bag of grain on Earth?
questions.explanation: Weight W = mg = 4 × 9.8 = 39.2 N.

questions.prompt: A constant force of 30 N drags a box 7 m in the direction of the force. How much work is done?
questions.explanation: Work W = F × d = 30 × 7 = 210 J.

questions.prompt: A force of 150 N acts on a surface of area 0.6 m². What pressure is produced?
Convert a temperature of 45 °C into kelvin.
Which substance type expands the most for the same rise in temperature?
questions.explanation: Gases expand most when heated, followed by liquids, then solids, because gas particles are freest to move apart.

questions.prompt: An object of density 950 kg/m³ is placed in water of density 1000 kg/m³. What will it do?
questions.explanation: An object floats if it is less dense than the fluid. 950 kg/m³ is less than 1000 kg/m³, so it floats.

questions.prompt: A 0.4 kg apple is held 1.5 m above the ground (g = 10 m/s²). What is its gravitational potential energy?
A van travelling at 16 m/s brakes at a constant 4 m/s². How long does it take to stop?
questions.explanation: Use v = u + at with v = 0 and a = -4: 0 = 16 + (-4)t, so t = 16 ÷ 4 = 4 s.

questions.prompt: A runner starts from rest and accelerates at 1.5 m/s² for 6 s. What distance is covered?

questions.topic: Force and Newton's Laws of Motion
questions.prompt: A 1500 kg car accelerates from rest to 24 m/s in 8 s. What net force acts on it?

questions.topic: Force and Newton's Laws of Motion
questions.prompt: A 3 kg box is pushed with a force of 25 N while a friction force of 7 N opposes it. What is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Net force = 25 - 7 = 18 N. Then a = F/m = 18 ÷ 3 = 6 m/s².

questions.prompt: A 0.2 kg arrow leaves a bow at 40 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
A crane lifts a 400 kg beam to a height of 9 m in 12 s (g = 10 m/s²). What is its useful power output?
Find the pressure at a depth of 15 m in fresh water (density 1000 kg/m³, g = 10 m/s²).
questions.explanation: Liquid pressure P = ρgh = 1000 × 10 × 15 = 150 000 Pa (150 kPa).

questions.prompt: A metal block has a mass of 810 g and a volume of 300 cm³. What is its density in kg/m³?
questions.explanation: Density = mass ÷ volume = 0.81 kg ÷ (300 × 10⁻⁶ m³) = 0.81 ÷ 0.0003 = 2700 kg/m³ (aluminium).

questions.prompt: Convert a temperature of 400 K into degrees Celsius.
A cup holding 200 g of tea at 90 °C and a bucket holding 10 kg of water at 30 °C are compared. Which statement is correct?
options: The tea has more heat energy because it is hotter
Both hold exactly the same heat energy
Heat would flow from the bucket to the tea
The bucket holds more heat energy despite its lower temperature
questions.explanation: Temperature is not the same as heat. The much larger mass of water in the bucket stores more total heat energy even though its temperature is lower.

questions.prompt: A bacterium has a length of 0.0000025 m. Written in scientific notation this is:
questions.explanation: Move the decimal point six places to the right to obtain 2.5, so 0.0000025 m = 2.5 × 10⁻⁶ m.

questions.prompt: A rectangular tank measures 0.2 m by 0.3 m by 0.5 m. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Volume = length × width × height = 0.2 × 0.3 × 0.5 = 0.03 m³.

questions.prompt: A 2 kg stone is dropped from a height of 20 m (g = 10 m/s²). Using energy conservation, what is its speed just before it lands?
questions.explanation: PE becomes KE: mgh = ½mv², so v² = 2gh = 2 × 10 × 20 = 400, giving v = 20 m/s (mass cancels).

questions.prompt: A sewing needle is pushed with a force of 5 N and its tip has an area of 0.0000005 m². What pressure does the tip exert?
questions.explanation: P = F ÷ A = 5 ÷ (5 × 10⁻⁷) = 1 × 10⁷ Pa. The tiny tip area gives an enormous pressure, so the needle pierces easily.

questions.prompt: A motorbike accelerates uniformly from 6 m/s to 24 m/s over a distance of 90 m. What is its acceleration?
questions.explanation: Use v² = u² + 2as: 24² = 6² + 2a(90), so 576 = 36 + 180a, giving 180a = 540 and a = 3 m/s².

questions.topic: Force and Newton's Laws of Motion
questions.prompt: When you walk forward, your foot pushes backward on the ground and you move forward. Which law explains this, and what provides the forward push?
options: First Law; inertia pushes you forward
Second Law; gravity gives the push
Third Law; the ground pushes your foot forward with an equal and opposite force
Third Law; friction is removed so you slide forward
questions.explanation: By Newton's Third Law, your foot pushes back on the ground (action) and the ground pushes your foot forward with an equal and opposite force (reaction), moving you forward.

questions.prompt: A pendulum bob is released from a height of 0.2 m above its lowest point. Using energy conservation (g = 10 m/s²), what is its speed at the lowest point?
questions.explanation: PE becomes KE: mgh = ½mv², so v² = 2gh = 2 × 10 × 0.2 = 4, giving v = 2 m/s (mass cancels).

questions.prompt: A vacuum flask keeps a drink hot by having a vacuum between its double walls. The vacuum is most effective at reducing heat loss by:
options: Conduction and convection, because both need particles
questions.explanation: Conduction and convection both need a material medium, so the vacuum (no particles) stops them. Radiation can still cross a vacuum, which is why the walls are also made shiny.
